'''''Mammillaria plumosa''''', the '''feather cactus''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[cactus| Cactaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to Northeastern Mexico.

It grows to {{convert|12|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|40|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad. The clustering spherical stems, {{convert|7|cm|0|abbr=on}} in diameter, are completely covered in white downy spines. The spines are adorned with very long hairs that are arranged like the segments of a bird's feather and protect the plant against the blistering sun of the desert. White or greenish yellow flowers are borne in late summer.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|pages=1136}}</ref>

Its status is listed as "Near Threatened" by the IUCN Red List.<ref name="iucn status 11 November 2021" /> 

==Cultivation==
''Mammillaria plumosa'' is one of several ''Mammillaria'' species to be cultivated.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cactus Art - ''Mammillaria plumosa''|url=http://www.cactus-art.biz/schede/MAMMILLARIA/Mammillaria_plumosa/Mammillaria_plumosa/Mammillaria_plumosa.htm|access-date=26 June 2013}}</ref> In [[temperateness|temperate]] regions it must be grown under glass with heat. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Mammillaria plumosa''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/10832/Mammillaria-plumosa/Details | access-date = 3 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
